title: Tempe Reconstruction & Rebuild After Damage | Gold Water Fire, Phoenix, AZ
description: Reconstruction and rebuild in Tempe, AZ after fire or water damage. Gold Water Fire rebuilds walls, floors, cabinets and finishes. Call (480) 999-3339.
intro: The demolition is done and now the house just sits there. Studs where the hallway wall used to be, plastic taped over a doorway, the kitchen sink sitting in the garage. Everyone who came out fast has come and gone, and what is left is the slow part: someone has to actually put the house back. You have been trying to keep the adjuster, the flooring quote, and your own family's schedule all straight in your head, and it is a lot to carry alone for weeks on end.

sections.heading: Tempe houses are built in ways that shape the rebuild
sections.body: Tempe is largely built out, and most of the residential stock went up between the 1950s and the early 1980s, filling in around Arizona State University: the postwar ranches near Maple-Ash and Wilson, the block-and-slab tracts south of Broadway, and the big 1970s subdivisions around The Lakes and Dobson Ranch's Tempe edge. That era matters when you rebuild. Slab-on-grade construction with no crawlspace means water spreads sideways under flooring instead of draining away, so restoring a floor often means the affected room and everything that shares the same continuous slab and threshold. Painted CMU block exterior walls, common in Tempe, do not take drywall patching the way a wood-framed wall does, and interior walls in these homes were often finished with a hand-textured or skip-trowel coat that has to be matched by feel, not ordered from a catalog. Older Tempe houses also tend to have original single-pane aluminum sliders, popcorn or acoustic ceilings, and cabinets built in place rather than dropped in as boxes, so a like-for-like rebuild is closer to carpentry than assembly.

cards.heading: Slab and flooring
cards.body: On slab-on-grade homes, moisture wicks into the concrete itself. Flooring that goes back down over a slab that still holds moisture will bubble, cup, or release its adhesive later, so slab readiness is checked before new material is set.

cards.heading: Texture and paint
cards.body: Matching a 1960s hand texture and a paint color that has sat in Arizona sun for years usually means feathering the repair well past the damaged area and repainting to a natural break, corner to corner, so the wall reads as one surface.

cards.heading: Cabinets and countertops
cards.body: Site-built cabinets in older Tempe kitchens rarely match anything current. Rebuilding may mean new boxes and doors made to the original openings so the run still fits the room.

sections.heading: Why Tempe rebuilds cluster after certain weeks
sections.body: The damage that leads to reconstruction in Tempe follows a pattern. Monsoon season from June into September brings microbursts that drive rain sideways under door thresholds and into scuppers and parapet details on the flat and low-slope roofs common on midcentury Tempe homes. Because so much of Tempe is flat and hard-surfaced, and because of the way the Rio Salado corridor and the older north Tempe streets collect runoff, water tends to sit at the front of a house and find its way in at the garage or a patio slider rather than pouring in from above. Winter brings the other half of it: a cold snap on an uninsulated or minimally insulated hose bib or a water heater sitting in an unconditioned garage, then a slow leak nobody hears for a day. Add the summer load on 40-year-old electrical and HVAC and you get the small fires that start in a laundry room, a garage panel, or an attic air handler. In all of those cases the mitigation crew opens up the affected assemblies, and the rebuild is what turns an opened-up house back into a home.

sections.heading: One crew carrying the rebuild end to end
sections.body: Gold Water Fire does mitigation and reconstruction, so the same company that dried or cleaned the structure can be the one that closes it back up. That matters mostly because nothing gets handed off at the worst moment. Brandon Gurr is our Construction Manager and leads the reconstruction and rebuild work, with Johnny as Reconstruction Team Lead running the job on site. Kristine handles the office side, and Brooke schedules water and mitigation work, so calls get answered by someone who knows your address. Jim Bennett and Jake Taylor co-founded the company. We hold AZ ROC license #264344, KB-2. Scope, documentation, and photos are put together in the form your insurance carrier expects, which is usually the part homeowners find hardest to do alone. sections.heading: Tempe and the surrounding metro
sections.body: We serve the full Phoenix metro area, roughly NW Peoria, SE Avondale, SW San Tan Valley, NW Apache Junction, and outlying areas further than that. In and around Tempe that includes the neighborhoods near ASU and Mill Avenue, south Tempe near the Chandler and Guadalupe lines, and the Papago and Rio Salado side toward Scottsdale and Phoenix. Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Scottsdale, and Phoenix are all inside the same working radius. You can reach us through the contact page or learn who you would be working with on the about page.

faqs.q: Can you rebuild if another company did the demolition and drying?
faqs.a: Yes. We often pick up a job after mitigation was done by someone else. We will want to see the moisture documentation and what was removed, and we will confirm the structure and the slab are dry and clean before new material goes back in. If that documentation does not exist, we verify conditions ourselves rather than assume.

faqs.q: Will the new drywall texture match the rest of my Tempe house?
faqs.a: That is the goal, and it takes hand work. Midcentury and 1970s Arizona homes usually have a troweled or knockdown texture applied by a person, so the repair is blended out from the patch and the wall is repainted to a corner or other natural stopping point. Perfectly invisible is not always possible on a wall with decades of sun on it, and we will tell you upfront where a wall or a whole room is the better call.

faqs.q: Do you handle the insurance paperwork for the rebuild?
faqs.a: We prepare the scope, line items, and photo documentation in the format carriers work from, and we communicate with your adjuster about the rebuild scope. The policy and the settlement are between you and your carrier, but you do not have to be the one translating construction into insurance language.

faqs.q: How long will my kitchen or bathroom be out of use?
faqs.a: It depends on the size of the loss, what has to be custom made, and how quickly the scope is approved. Site-built cabinets, discontinued tile, and slab drying all add time. We give you a sequence and the milestones for your specific job at the start, and tell you when something changes instead of leaving you guessing.

cta.heading: Let someone else carry the rebuild
cta.body: You have already done the hardest part, which was getting through the first days of this. Putting the house back does not have to be yours to figure out. Call Gold Water Fire at (480) 999-3339 or email Help@goldwaterfire.com, tell us the address in Tempe and what has been opened up, and we will walk the job with you and lay out what the rebuild actually involves.
